hints.title: Parent Pointer Traversal Path
hints.text: When nodes contain parent references, the next sequential node depends solely on the presence of a right branch or ancestry steps.

hints.title: Two Case Successor Branching
hints.text: If a right child exists, find the leftmost node in that right subtree. Otherwise, climb parent pointers until finding an ancestor of which the current node is in the left branch.

hints.title: Step-by-Step Traversal Blueprint
hints.text: If node.right: curr = node.right; while curr.left: curr = curr.left; return curr. Else: curr = node; while curr.parent and curr == curr.parent.right: curr = curr.parent; return curr.parent.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: H: height of the binary search tree
complexity.notes: Traverses either down to the leftmost leaf or up ancestors, bound by tree height H.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Traversing the entire tree from the root takes O(N) time and requires root access which is unavailable.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant auxiliary space utilizing parent pointers directly.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clear identification of the two cases: right subtree minimum vs ancestor traversal.

solutions.approach: Right Subtree Descent or Ancestor Climb
